observations.semantic_recognizability: The production three-quarter and profile images show a desk with a separate monitor setup.
observations.silhouette_quality: Two end columns and the floor-level cross feet now form a clear standing-desk T-frame; the tabletop remains thin.
observations.proportion: The validator measured 66 x 29.97 x 30 inches. The 0.03-inch y offset is the rubber leveler base and remains within the brief's proportion tolerance.
observations.geometric_detail: The close view shows lift columns, broad feet, a rear crossbar, glass mounts, edge band, and control pad; several details remain simple low-poly shapes.
observations.material_realism: The top is brighter than v2 and has a specular highlight, but still looks opaque and nearly uniform from most camera angles.
observations.surface_variation: The top, edge band, columns, and feet separate by color and roughness; the wide glass plane has little visible tonal variation.
observations.close_up_quality: The profile and underside detail clearly show the T feet and rectangular columns while real room objects remain present.
observations.gameplay_readability: The desk and its independently defined monitors remain recognizable in the room view.
observations.scale_fidelity: The asset remains within the brief's 20% source-proportion tolerance and matches the 66 x 30 x 30-inch RoomDefinition envelope.
observations.art_direction_fit: The open support frame matches the modern workstation and remains compatible with the room's stylized rendering.
observations.technical_integration: Godot imported 19 meshes and 19 surfaces; the production resolver loaded desk-v003 and the production renders completed at 55 FPS in the final detail view.
observations.source_resemblance: The two lift columns and broad depth-spanning T feet now match the photographed standing-desk construction; the opaque top still falls short of the visible glass surface.

defects: The smoked-glass surface still reads as opaque gray material rather than glass over the frame.
Only a small localized reflection is visible on the otherwise uniform desktop.
likely_causes: The top is exported as an opaque StandardMaterial3D, so monitors, frame, and room light cannot show through it.
The room lighting produces only a point-like specular glint on the broad plane.
next_action_hypothesis: Keep the accepted T-frame geometry and change only the glass material recipe: add controlled alpha transparency with opaque-only depth drawing, retain the dark tint, increase clearcoat, and add a slim satin edge band. This should reveal the support structure through the glass and create a readable glass edge without changing any bounds or room data.
incumbent_comparison: Better than desk-v002 on standing-desk silhouette, source resemblance, and floor-foot construction; current best-so-far candidate, but material realism is still below the promotion threshold.
